mainTopic: מוקצה and fire on יום טוב: using wood for other jobs, firebrands, gathering kindling, and producing new fire
overview: This amud first finishes a list of household items that follow one rule on יום טוב: hold the top piece first, then put the support underneath. The גמרא then quotes the משנה that one may not prop a pot with a piece of firewood. It corrects the wording so that a door is also something that may not be propped with wood. A ברייתא explains that wood is meant only for burning, so other uses are מוקצה, while רבי שמעון permits. The ברייתא also forbids leading an animal with a stick. The גמרא explains that the reason is not מוקצה but that it looks like a weekday trip to market. רב נחמן and רב ששת argue about roasting with a reed, and the גמרא reports the argument in two versions. The הלכה is that a dry reed is permitted and a wet reed is forbidden. רבא forbids taking a firebrand from the woodshed and burning a broken one, and the גמרא shows he holds of מוקצה even though he gave duck innards to his cat. A new משנה follows. It records an argument over gathering kindling from the courtyard, and it forbids producing new fire or heating tiles white-hot to roast on. The גמרא's discussion begins with רב יהודה.

steps.title: More cases that follow the same rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a list from just before: eggs, a pot, a bed, and barrels all follow the same rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same applies to eggs, to a pot, to a bed, and to barrels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list from just before. These four items all follow the same rule: hold the top piece in place first, and only then put the supports underneath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this point, the גמרא gave a rule that the top must be held up first and the supports added below it. Here it simply adds four more everyday examples. Nothing new is argued; the rule is just applied more widely.

keyTerms.meaning: A bed (one that comes apart into pieces)

phrases.english: And similarly eggs, and similarly a pot,
and similarly a bed, and similarly barrels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list from the end of the previous section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eggs, a pot, a bed, and barrels all follow the rule that the top is held first and the support is added underneath afterward.

steps.title: The משנה: do not prop a pot with wood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: one may not prop a pot with a piece of wood, and the same goes for a door.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: One may not prop a pot with a piece of wood, and the same goes for a door.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה. This sets up the next move, because the wording about the door is about to be questioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids using a piece of firewood to hold a pot steady on יום טוב. The words 'and similarly with a door' sound odd, and the גמרא will deal with that right away.

phrases.english: And one may not prop a pot with a piece of wood,
and similarly with a door.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pot may not be propped with a piece of wood on יום טוב.

steps.title: Who props a pot with a door?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how anyone could think of propping a pot with a door.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a door? Could that possibly enter your mind?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the משנה. Nobody holds up a pot with a whole door, so 'with a door' cannot be what the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about wording, not about the law. Read plainly, the משנה seems to say the door is used to prop the pot, which makes no practical sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? (a way of saying the idea makes no sense)

phrases.english: With a door, can that enter your mind?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the משנה quoted in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'וכן בדלת' in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A pot is never propped with a door, so the words as written make no sense.

steps.title: Fixing the wording: the door is what gets propped
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the משנה to read 'and similarly a door', meaning one may not prop a door with a piece of wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: and similarly a door.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording. The משנה means that a door, just like a pot, may not be propped up with a piece of wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing 'with a door' to 'a door' turns the door into the thing being propped, not the thing doing the propping. The same law now covers both a pot and a door.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (used to fix the wording)

phrases.english: Rather, say: and similarly a door.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say a door is used to prop a pot.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means a door, like a pot, may not be propped with a piece of wood.

steps.title: The reason: wood is only for burning
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that wood may not be used to prop a pot or a door because wood is set aside only for burning, while רבי שמעון permits.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One may not prop a pot with a piece of wood, and the same goes for a door, because wood was given only for burning. And רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא gives the reason for the משנה's rule. Firewood is meant only for burning, so using it for anything else is not allowed, but רבי שמעון disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since firewood is set aside for burning, using it for another job makes it מוקצה for that use. רבי שמעון does not hold of this kind of מוקצה, so he permits propping with it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that wood is only for burning returns at the end of this section as רב נחמן's reason.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may not prop a pot with a piece of wood,
and similarly a door,
because wood was not given
except for burning.
And Rabbi Shimon permits it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין סוֹמְכִין אֶת הַקְּדֵרָה בַּבְּקַעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that repeats the corrected wording and gives its reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wood is only for burning, so it is מוקצה for other uses. רבי שמעון permits.

steps.title: Leading an animal with a stick
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: one may not lead an animal with a stick on יום טוב, but רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not lead an animal with a stick on יום טוב, but רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds another case involving a stick: guiding an animal with it on יום טוב. The תנא קמא forbids it and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון permits it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This also seems to be a case of using wood for something other than burning. That is why the גמרא will next ask whether רבי אלעזר is simply following his father's view on מוקצה.

phrases.english: And one may not lead an animal
with a stick on a Festival,
and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon permits it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין מַנְהִיגִין אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה בַּמַּקֵּל בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא forbids leading an animal with a stick on יום טוב. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון permits it.

steps.title: Does the son follow his father on מוקצה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי אלעזר permits because, like his father רבי שמעון, he does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds like his father, who does not hold of מוקצה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a reason for רבי אלעזר's leniency: maybe he simply follows his father רבי שמעון, who does not forbid מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling in step 5 showed that רבי שמעון permits using wood for other jobs. It would make sense for his son to permit the stick for the same reason. The גמרא puts this forward as a suggestion and will test it next.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion the גמרא may reject)
Something set aside that may not be moved or used on שבת or יום טוב

steps.confusionAlert: A question starting with לֵימָא is usually a suggestion that the גמרא is about to reject, so don't treat it as the final answer.

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon
holds like his father,
who does not hold of מוקצה?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן כַּאֲבוּהּ סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the dispute in step 6, linking it to רבי שמעון in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רבי אלעזר's leniency based on rejecting מוקצה, as his father does?

steps.title: No, it looks like going to the market
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion: here even רבי שמעון agrees it is forbidden, because it looks like going to the market.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. In this case even רבי שמעון agrees, because it looks like someone going to the market.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that this dispute is about מוקצה. The reason to forbid is different: leading an animal with a stick looks like taking it to market on a regular weekday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the problem is how it looks, and not מוקצה, even רבי שמעון would forbid it. So רבי אלעזר's leniency cannot simply come from his father's view on מוקצה.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, בְּהָא אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מוֹדֶה,
phrases.english: No, in this case even Rabbi Shimon agrees,
because it looks
like someone who is going to the market.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, בְּהָא אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מוֹדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the stick dispute depends on מוקצה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The reason to forbid is that it looks like a weekday market trip, a concern that even רבי שמעון accepts.

steps.title: Roasting with a reed: רב נחמן vs. רב ששת
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן forbids using a reed (to roast with), and רב ששת permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A reed: רב נחמן forbids it and רב ששת permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new argument begins between אמוראים about using a reed branch on יום טוב. רב נחמן forbids it and רב ששת permits it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasons given right after this show that the reed is being used to roast meat. Again the question is whether wood may be used for something other than burning.

phrases.english: A reed: Rav Nachman forbids it,
and Rav Sheshet permits it.

steps.triggerLanguage: חִזְרָא, רַב נַחְמָן אָסַר, וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת שָׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new argument connected to the theme of using wood for other jobs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן forbids using a reed; רב ששת permits it.

steps.title: Wet reed: everyone forbids; the argument is about dry
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees a wet reed is forbidden. They argue only about a dry reed.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a wet reed, everyone agrees it is forbidden. They argue about a dry one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the argument. A wet reed is forbidden by both, so the dispute is only about a dry reed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wet reed can't be burned, so it has no permitted use at all. A dry reed can be burned, and that is what opens the door to an argument.

phrases.english: With a wet one, everyone
does not argue that it is forbidden.
Where they argue is with a dry one.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרַטִּיבָא כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּאָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the exact case of the dispute in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wet reed is forbidden by all; the dispute is limited to a dry reed.

steps.title: רב נחמן's reason: wood is only for burning
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן forbids because wood is given only for burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who forbids will tell you: wood was given only for burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב נחמן's side. He uses the same reason as the ברייתא: wood is only for burning, so using it as a roasting stick is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though a dry reed may be burned, roasting meat on it is a different use. For רב נחמן, that other use makes it מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Will tell you (gives that side's reasoning)

phrases.english: The one who forbids will tell you:
Wood was given only for burning.
phrases.notes: These are the same words as the ברייתא in step 5.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning of the stricter side in the dry-reed case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wood may be used only for burning, so roasting on a reed is forbidden.

steps.title: רב ששת's reason: roasting is roasting
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת permits: roasting with the reed itself is no different from roasting over its coals.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who permits will tell you: What difference is it to me whether I roast with it or roast with its coals?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב ששת's side. Burning the reed and roasting over its coals is allowed, and roasting with the reed itself is the same kind of use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת agrees that wood is set aside for burning, but he sees burning as being for cooking. Using the reed directly to roast serves the same cooking purpose, so it is not a forbidden other use.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference is it to me (both cases are the same)

steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, a wet reed is forbidden by all. For a dry reed, רב נחמן forbids, because wood is only for burning, and רב ששת permits, because roasting with it is the same as roasting over its coals. (The next step gives a second version.)

phrases.english: And the one who permits will tell you:
What difference is it to me to roast with it,
or to roast with its coals?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the lenient side's answer, responding to רב נחמן's reason in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Roasting with a dry reed is permitted, because it serves the same purpose as roasting over its coals.

steps.title: A second version of the argument: dry is fine, wet is disputed
steps.stepSummary: איכא דאמרי: everyone permits a dry reed, and רב נחמן and רב ששת argue only about a wet one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it the other way: with a dry reed, everyone agrees it is permitted. They only argue about a wet reed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different report of the argument between רב נחמן and רב ששת. In this version the dry reed is permitted by everyone, and the argument is only about a wet one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (Step 10), everyone forbade a wet reed and they argued about a dry one. Here the line moves over: everyone permits a dry reed, and the wet reed is the one in question. So the area of argument has shifted.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say, introducing a second version of what was said
A dry one (dry reed or stick)
A wet one (moist, fresh reed or stick)
Everyone agrees; there is no argument

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In the first version, wet is forbidden by all and dry is disputed. In this version, dry is permitted by all and wet is disputed.

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: בְּיַבִּשְׁתָּא — כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דִּשְׁרֵי.
phrases.english: With a dry one, everyone agrees that it is permitted.
When they argue, it is about a wet one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of where the argument from Steps 9-12 lies
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, a dry reed is permitted by all, and only a wet reed is disputed.

steps.title: The reasons in the second version: not fit to burn versus fit for a big fire
steps.stepSummary: The one who forbids says a wet reed cannot burn. The one who permits says a big fire can still burn it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who forbids says it is not fit for burning. The one who permits would tell you: it is fit for a big fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason of each side in the second version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one who forbids says a wet reed is not fit to be fuel, so it has no permitted use on יום טוב. The one who permits answers that in a big fire even a wet reed will dry out and burn, so it does count as usable fuel.

phrases.english: The one who forbids: because it is not fit for burning.
And the one who permits would tell you:
But it is fit for a big fire!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind both sides of the second version
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forbidder: a wet reed is not fuel. Permitter: in a big fire it still counts as fuel.

steps.title: The final ruling: dry permitted, wet forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה: a dry reed is permitted and a wet reed is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: a dry one is permitted, a wet one is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling on the reed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling permits the dry reed, which everyone allows in the second version. It forbids the wet reed, which everyone forbids in the first version. So the הלכה follows the stricter view on the wet reed.
steps.whatToRemember: Bottom line for roasting with a reed on יום טוב: a dry reed is allowed, a wet reed is not.

phrases.english: And the הלכה is: a dry one is permitted,
a wet one is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the argument from both versions with a practical ruling
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A dry reed is permitted and a wet reed is forbidden.

steps.title: רבא's teaching about a firebrand
steps.stepSummary: רבא: a woman may not take a firebrand from the woodshed, and a broken firebrand may not be burned, because one burns utensils but not broken pieces of utensils.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: A woman may not go into the woodshed to take a firebrand from there. And a firebrand that broke may not be burned on יום טוב, because one may burn utensils but not broken pieces of utensils.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא teaches two rules about an אוד, a half-burnt stick used to stir a fire, on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First rule: she may not take an אוד from the woodshed. Second rule: an אוד counts as a utensil, so it may be burned while whole. Once it breaks, it becomes a broken piece of a utensil and may not be used as fuel on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A firebrand, a half-burnt stick used to stir the fire

phrases.english: רבא taught publicly:
A woman may not go into the woodshed
to take a firebrand from them.
And a firebrand that broke
may not be burned on יום טוב,
because one may burn with utensils,
but one may not burn with broken pieces of utensils.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: rules about a firebrand on יום טוב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not take a firebrand from the woodshed, and do not burn a broken firebrand on יום טוב.

steps.title: Does רבא hold of מוקצה? He gave duck innards to a cat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבא holds like רבי יהודה, who accepts מוקצה, since רבא told his attendant to throw duck innards to the cat on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean רבא holds like רבי יהודה, who accepts מוקצה? But רבא told his attendant: Roast me a duck and throw its innards to the cat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads רבא's rules as based on מוקצה. It then points out a story that seems to show רבא does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבא forbids the firebrand because of מוקצה, he is following רבי יהודה. But according to רבי יהודה, the duck's innards were not set aside for the cat before יום טוב, so giving them to it should be forbidden. Yet רבא did exactly that, so the two seem to contradict.

keyTerms.meaning: Something not set aside for use before שבת or יום טוב, so it may not be used

phrases.english: Is that to say that רבא
holds like רבי יהודה,
who holds of מוקצה?
But רבא said to his attendant:
Roast me a duck
and throw its innards to the cat!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרָבָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's teaching by setting it against his own conduct
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבא holds of מוקצה like רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא gave duck innards to a cat on יום טוב, which רבי יהודה would forbid as מוקצה. So רבא seems not to hold of מוקצה.

steps.title: The innards were already in mind the day before
steps.stepSummary: Innards go bad quickly, so even before יום טוב רבא already planned to give them to the cat. This means there is no מוקצה there.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, since innards go bad, from yesterday his mind was already on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. The duck case is different, so רבא can still hold of מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Innards spoil fast, so a person knows ahead of time that they will go to the animals. Because רבא had them in mind for the cat before יום טוב, they were never מוקצה. So רבא can follow רבי יהודה, and the firebrand rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: His mind was on them, he planned to use them

steps.whatToRemember: רבא does hold of מוקצה. The innards were allowed only because he had them in mind for the cat before יום טוב.

phrases.english: There, since they go bad,
from yesterday his mind was on them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by showing the duck case is different
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Giving innards to the cat shows רבא does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Innards spoil, so he set them aside for the cat before יום טוב. They were never מוקצה, and רבא can still hold like רבי יהודה.

steps.title: New משנה: taking a splinter and gathering kindling
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר: one may take a splinter to pick his teeth and gather kindling from the courtyard, because the whole courtyard counts as prepared. The חכמים: one may gather only from what is in front of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי אליעזר says: A person may take a splinter from what is in front of him to pick his teeth. And he may gather from the courtyard and light a fire, because everything in the courtyard counts as prepared. The חכמים say: He may gather only from what is in front of him and light it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It brings an argument about how far 'prepared for use' reaches on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר says everything in the courtyard counts as ready for use, so one may gather sticks from there for a fire. The חכמים limit it to what is right in front of the person. Things scattered in the courtyard were not in his mind before יום טוב, so they are not prepared.

keyTerms.meaning: A splinter, a small chip of wood or straw
Prepared, ready for use (the opposite of מוקצה)

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'from what is in front of him' appears for both sides. רבי אליעזר uses it for the splinter and also allows gathering from the courtyard. The חכמים allow gathering only from what is in front of him.

phrases.english: משנה: רבי אליעזר says:
A person may take a splinter from what is in front of him,
to pick his teeth with it.
And he may gather from the courtyard and light,
for everything in the courtyard is prepared.
And the חכמים say:
He gathers from what is in front of him and lights.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה, continuing the theme of מוקצה and what counts as prepared
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: the courtyard is fully prepared, so one may take a splinter and gather kindling there. חכמים: one may gather only from what is in front of him.

steps.title: No producing new fire and no whitening tiles on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that on יום טוב one may not produce fire from wood, stones, dirt, tiles, or water. One also may not heat tiles until white-hot in order to roast on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may not make fire on יום טוב, not from wood, stones, dirt, tiles, or water. You also may not heat tiles until they turn white-hot in order to roast food on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two new rules. You may not create a brand-new fire on יום טוב, and you may not heat tiles until white-hot to roast on them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using an existing fire on יום טוב for cooking is allowed. This משנה forbids producing a new fire from five different sources. The second rule is a separate case: preparing tiles by heating them until they glow white, so they can later be used for roasting.

keyTerms.meaning: Producing fire, literally 'bringing out the fire.' This means making a new flame.
Heating something until it glows white-hot.

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה does not forbid all fire on יום טוב. Cooking with a fire that already exists is permitted. The משנה is talking about producing a new fire.

phrases.english: One may not produce fire
neither from wood,
nor from stones,
nor from dirt,
nor from tiles,
nor from water.
phrases.notes: Water in a round glass vessel can focus the sun's rays and start a fire, like a magnifying glass.

phrases.english: And one may not whiten tiles
phrases.notes: 'Whiten' means heating the tiles until they glow white-hot.

phrases.english: to roast upon them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מוֹצִיאִין אֶת הָאוּר לֹא מִן הָעֵצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the next part of the same משנה passage that began in step 19, before the גמרא starts. It moves from gathering wood and kindling to producing fire itself and preparing tiles.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב one may not produce new fire from wood, stones, dirt, tiles, or water. One may not heat tiles until white-hot in order to roast on them.

steps.title: The גמרא opens with a statement from רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by introducing a statement from רב יהודה. His actual words come at the start of the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יהודה said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא starts discussing the משנה and introduces רב יהודה, whose statement comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening words are here: the marker for the start of the גמרא and the name רב יהודה. Nothing has been ruled or explained yet. The content of his statement will be the real next move.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה.
A leading אמורא, a student of רב and שמואל.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Yehuda said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This begins the גמרא's discussion of the משנה from step 20 by bringing in an אמורא's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not stated yet. This line only introduces רב יהודה's statement, which follows.
